title: Alcohol withdrawal
stem: Cubicle 3. Mr Tse, 48, drinks a bottle of spirits a day and stopped 30 hours ago because he ran out of money. He is sweaty and shaking and says he can see spiders on the wall. HR 124, BP 164/98, temperature 37.9 °C. Assess and manage him.

phases.title: Assess
phases.goal: Monitoring, the drinking history, and examine him yourself: Wernicke's?

phases.title: Treat
phases.goal: Thiamine before glucose, and a benzodiazepine, from the cart. Promptly.

phases.title: Work-up
phases.goal: Bloods and imaging for what alcohol hides.

events.say: He has a generalised withdrawal seizure.
events.untreated: He had a withdrawal seizure and was never given a benzodiazepine.

review.text: Thiamine dose. Your notes give thiamine 100 mg IV. For suspected Wernicke's encephalopathy, UK practice uses high-dose parenteral thiamine (Pabrinex, 2 pairs three times a day for 3–5 days). 'Thiamine before glucose' is sensible, but never delay treating hypoglycaemia for it.

notes:
Checked against NICE CG100 (Alcohol-use disorders: physical complications, 2010, updated 2017), NICE CG115, and the CIWA-Ar.

Withdrawal: tremor, sweating, anxiety, tachycardia (6–24 h); seizures (12–48 h); delirium tremens (48–72 h): confusion, hallucinations (often visual or tactile), autonomic instability; mortality without treatment. Treat with a benzodiazepine (chlordiazepoxide or diazepam) by a symptom-triggered regimen guided by CIWA-Ar, or a fixed-dose reducing regimen; lorazepam if liver failure. Delirium tremens: IV/oral benzodiazepine titrated; haloperidol only as an adjunct; phenobarbital in refractory cases.

Wernicke's encephalopathy (confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia — the triad is incomplete in most): give parenteral thiamine (Pabrinex) before glucose where possible, high dose (e.g. 2 pairs of Pabrinex three times daily for 3–5 days if suspected; prophylactic 1 pair daily if at risk). Check glucose, electrolytes (magnesium, phosphate, potassium), and look for head injury, sepsis, GI bleeding and pancreatitis.

Your notes: thiamine 100 mg IV — UK practice uses Pabrinex doses higher than that for suspected Wernicke's; 'always thiamine before glucose' is sensible but never delay treating hypoglycaemia. CAGE and CIWA-Ar descriptions match.

Perfect script checked against NICE CG100 alcohol withdrawal, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed oral thiamine and discharge, an IV diazepam bolus, and haloperidol alone; Wernicke's named aloud.

steps.label: Monitoring
steps.hint: Ask the nurse to put the patient on the monitor.

opts.t: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2, and a capillary glucose.
opts.mark: Asks for continuous ECG, NIBP and SpO2 monitoring

steps.label: History
steps.hint: Quantity, last drink, previous withdrawal, seizures, DTs, other substances, injuries, symptoms.

Drinking.t: How much do you drink, and when was your last drink?
Drinking.tz: 你平時飲幾多酒？上一次飲係幾時？
Drinking.rz: 飲咗好多年，一日一支威士忌。上次飲係琴日朝早。
Drinking.r: A bottle of whisky a day for years. Last drink yesterday morning.
Drinking.mark: Quantifies alcohol and time of last drink

Drinking.t: Have you had fits or DTs when stopping before?
Drinking.tz: 以前戒酒嗰陣有冇抽過筋，或者出現震顫性譫妄？
Drinking.rz: 上次戒嗰陣抽過一次筋。
Drinking.r: I had a fit last time I stopped.
Drinking.mark: Asks about previous withdrawal seizures or DTs

Drinking.tz: 有冇用其他藥物，或者食安眠藥？

Now.rz: 有好多蜘蛛喺牆上面，仲爬上我隻手。
Now.r: Spiders crawling on the wall and on my arms.

Now.t: Any vomiting blood, belly pain, falls or head injury?
Now.tz: 有冇嘔血、肚痛？有冇跌親或者撞到個頭？
Now.rz: 冇嘔血。上個禮拜跌親，撞到個頭。
Now.r: No blood. Fell last week, hit my head.
Now.mark: Screens for GI bleeding and head injury

steps.label: Examine
steps.hint: Orientation, eyes, gait, tremor, liver, head.

Neuro.r: Disorientated to date and place, inattentive.
Wide-based and unsteady. "Confusion, nystagmus and ataxia: Wernicke's encephalopathy, with delirium tremens."

General.r: Spider naevi, liver edge 3 cm. Old bruise on the occiput.
General.mark: Looks for liver disease and head injury

steps.label: Drug cart
steps.hint: Thiamine before glucose; a benzodiazepine titrated to CIWA-Ar.

opts.mark: High-dose parenteral thiamine for suspected Wernicke's
opts.t: Pabrinex (high-dose thiamine) 2 pairs IV three times a day
opts.dose: 2 pairs IV three times a day

opts.t: Diazepam 10–20 mg orally, titrated to CIWA-Ar
Bloods: glucose, magnesium, phosphate, potassium, LFTs, FBC and lipase.
A CT head: he fell and hit his head, and he's alcohol-dependent.
He's admitted: delirium tremens and Wernicke's, with CIWA-Ar monitoring.
opts.mark: Admits for delirium tremens and Wernicke's

wrong: 1–2 hours after the last drink, as the level falls
Within 6 hours, while the alcohol level is still high
Glucose inactivates thiamine in the drip
Thiamine is absorbed better when fasting

badge.name: Dry Spell
badge.flavor: Pabrinex before sugar, benzos by CIWA, look for the head injury.

options: Within 1 hour of the last drink, while still drunk
2–3 weeks after stopping, as a late effect
Screen for alcohol dependence in primary care

cards.why: 2 or more positive answers is significant.

cards.q: Suspected Wernicke's in the UK is treated with…

options: Olfactory hallucinations only, such as burning

cards.q: Electrolyte often low in alcohol dependence?

script.say: Monitoring on, please: ECG, blood pressure and SpO2, and a capillary glucose.
How much do you drink, and when was your last drink? Have you had fits or DTs when stopping before? Any other drugs, sleeping tablets?
script.do: A bottle of whisky a day for years. Last drink yesterday morning. I had a fit last time I stopped. No.

script.say: What are you seeing? Any vomiting blood, belly pain, falls or head injury?
script.do: Spiders crawling on the wall and on my arms. No blood. Fell last week, hit my head.

script.say: Orientation and attention. Eye movements. Gait. Confusion, nystagmus and ataxia: Wernicke's encephalopathy, with delirium tremens.
script.do: Disorientated to date and place, inattentive. Horizontal nystagmus, weak lateral gaze. Wide-based and unsteady. "Confusion, nystagmus and ataxia: Wernicke's encephalopathy, with delirium tremens."
Coarse tremor of outstretched hands. Spider naevi, liver edge 3 cm. Old bruise on the occiput.

script.say: Pabrinex (high-dose thiamine) 2 pairs IV three times a day. Diazepam 10–20 mg orally, titrated to CIWA-Ar.

Bloods: glucose, magnesium, phosphate, potassium, LFTs, FBC and lipase. A CT head: he fell and hit his head, and he's alcohol-dependent. He's admitted: delirium tremens and Wernicke's, with CIWA-Ar monitoring.
